rationale: Round 1 built and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so weights are pushed upward to raise reverse-engineering resistance while respecting this program's profile: it is a tiny (1427 text bytes, 6 functions) floating-point compute kernel dominated by hot numeric loops (mandel-2, fbench, whetstone, flops family), so SUB stays near-max since it transforms arithmetic cheaply with low runtime and size cost and pairs well with the FP-heavy code; IGV is weighted high because it maximizes diversity across the few functions present and is cheap at runtime; SPLIT and IBR get moderate-to-high weights as low-cost structural diversifiers that make the small functions harder to match against reference builds; BCF and FLA keep solid security weights but their RuntimeCost and SizeCost entries stay elevated so the per-function feature matching spares the hottest inner loops, limiting worst-case slowdown on this compute-bound benchmark; ICALL is kept at a moderate weight since indirect calls add useful dispatch indirection but can disturb branch prediction in tight FP loops; overall CorrectnessRisk weights remain low-to-moderate because round 1 showed no correctness or compilation issues, giving headroom to accept slightly riskier transformations.
